title: Does .bss arrive zeroed? (follow-up to the big review)
summary: Yes, since PR #61 (2e8e2924, 2026-08-08): the kernel's .bss is zero at kmain on every shipped load path, by layout and not by instruction (KIMG_PARA includes KBSS_SIZE and .ovl's start= makes NASM emit the .bss range as zero padding; stage 2, kz_all or kz_hd lands it), checked on all three built kernels and their packed kernel.sys. Before kmain it is not zero (under KZIP it holds the packed stream), .lowbss is zero except dsk_secbuf's .ovl spill on shipped kernels and unloaded on NO_ROM_COLD, and .vgabuf is not zero. Module, driver and package bss each have their own (working) mechanism. The tree's behaviour is uniform; its wording is mixed: 65 false or arm-blind statements get exact fixes. No code defect; the gap is that nothing gates the zero range, and a fast-tier host check of kernel.bin over [text+bss_vstart, +bss_len) is recommended at 0 resident bytes.

findings.claim: Kernel .bss is zero at kmain on every shipped load path (kern_big/small/mega/emu; KZIP and NOKZIP; floppy, hard disk, live media; ROM/HMA .cold; every warm restart).
findings.evidence: kernel.asm:1679 (KIMG_PARA includes KBSS_SIZE), kernel.asm:2183 (.ovl start=OVL_START); build/*/kernel-full.bin has 0 non-zero bytes over the .bss range (0xB788..0xCC7E big, 0x8B53..0x96CB small, 0xCFFC..0xE518 mega); kernel.sys tails decode back to kernel.bin; boot2.asm:488 kz_all before :514 jmp; boothd.asm:293 via kz_hd; only three jmp KERNEL_SEG:0 sites.

findings.claim: Before kmain .bss is NOT zero: under KZIP it holds the packed LZ4 tail (KERNEL_SEG:0x5A00..0x17AB0 on kern_big) until kz_all; on NOKZIP it is unlanded RAM. Stage-2/splash state must live in the plain head (KERNEL_SEG:0..KZ_HEADSEC*512 = 4,608 B).
findings.evidence: build/kernel.kz.json rpara=1152, head=4608; viddet.inc:1022-1078 refuses stores past the head on the splash's first tick after the kern_small 1.44MB ui_post defect; boot2.asm:393 writes spl_fseg (0x669, head) before kz_all.

findings.claim: .lowbss is mixed: zero padding on shipped ROM_COLD kernels except dsk_secbuf (.ovl overruns the FAT window by 511/450/510 bytes on big/small/mega); not loaded at all on NO_ROM_COLD. Nothing promises it.
findings.evidence: kernel.asm:1687-1699 COLD_RAM=LOW_SEG+LOW_PARA; map: .ovl 0x13FF vs FAT 0x1200 (big), 0x5C2 vs 0x400 (small).

findings.claim: .vgabuf is not zero: .cfx's bytes on kern_big (by design), stale RAM on kern_mega; its only reader fills it first.

Sibling bss: module bss zero per fresh load via MODB_TAIL except CTRL.DRV's core-only read and a still-resident module; driver bss zeroed by drv_bss; package bss zeroed by ld_start step 7 (re-home path carries its own zeros in the part); kerndos zeroes its own .bss/.lowbss.
Investigator B's C-package off-by-one (last .bss byte unzeroed) is already fixed: CC_IMAGE_END's `align 2` before cc_image_end; B read crt0.asm's header describing the pre-fix bug.
NOKZIP .bss is fully zero (B's 'partly' refuted): no splash write lands in .bss during the load; bvs_apply's SS test refuses it and the splash's own state is cs:-relative or in the head.

Code relies on zero .bss with no init: sch_chbusy, evq_head/tail/count (no evq_init), loader state (no loader_init), clip_kb/clip_bytes, ui_tclkw, ui_armw, mem_cp_msk, fcp_made, dock_ck, mod_fp slots before kmain_o.
findings.evidence: sched.inc:2163/2201/2228/610, events.inc:62, kernel.asm:5904/5820, clip.inc:263/321, ui.inc:1661/3276, memory.inc:4059, filecp.inc:1695, dock.inc:140.

findings.claim: No gate checks that kernel.bin is zero over .bss; t_bsssentinel (soak) checks only non-zero sentinels. A layout that left .bss as the file's tail would silently restore pre-#61 behaviour, visible only on real hardware (emulators power on zeroed).
findings.recommendation: Add tests/unit/t_bsszero.py (fast tier): per built kernel, parse kernel.map for .text file start and .bss vstart/len, assert kernel.bin covers the range and every byte is 0; rely on os88kz.py:76-79's existing round-trip check for kernel.sys. Break it on purpose once in a private tree. Cost: 0 resident and 0 image bytes, ~40 lines, ~50 ms per make.

findings.claim: tests/tickzero.py guards a hazard that cannot occur on today's layout: dirty power-on RAM never reaches [ticks] (the load overwrites it) and nothing writes [ticks] between kz_all and sched_init. The row still detects the store's deletion because it plants junk after the load. Premise text corrected; the row itself is not wrong.

About 40 comments and SPEC passages still give pre-#61 rationale. 65 statements that are FALSE ('not zeroed', 'garbage', 'previous session's bytes', 'no image bytes', two that cite §12.8.5.1 for its opposite) or that name one arm's mechanism as the rule are fixed exactly; ~30 bare '-f bin zeroes nothing' rationales are literally true and harmless and are listed in the report, not fixed.
